quick.summary: How to test a new model safely without risking the entire user base.
quick.takeaway: Test with a tiny group first to limit the blast radius.

beats.line: My new spam filter blocked real messages. How do I test it safely?
Think of a chef trying a new soup recipe.
They do not serve a whole pot to the room.
Right. They ask one waiter to taste a spoon.
Exactly. We do that with code. It is a canary deployment.
Can I just say testing with a tiny group?
Yes. Testing with a tiny group.
You send one percent of visitors to the new filter.
If it fails, only a few people see a problem.
So I let a small group try it. Then expand if it works.
You catch mistakes early and most customers stay happy.

quiz.question: How should you test a new feature safely in production?
options: Give it to a tiny fraction of users.
Only test it on developer laptops.
Send it to everyone but warn them first.
quiz.explanation: Testing with a small percentage of users limits the damage if something goes wrong.

quiz.question: A canary deployment means rolling back to an older version of your code.
quiz.explanation: A canary deployment is about releasing new code to a very small group first, not rolling back.
